sections.title: Level 3 Advanced Overview
sections.content: At Level 3, phrasal verbs appear in more complex forms. These include three-part phrasal verbs, the use of two phrasal verbs within a single sentence, less common phrasal verbs, and particle errors in complex sentences. To solve these questions, it is necessary to understand context, grammatical structure, and logical meaning together.

sections.title: Three-part Phrasal Verbs (Verb + Adverb + Preposition)
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the verb. Step 2: Check whether it is followed by two particles (an adverb and a preposition). Step 3: Understand the entire phrasal verb as a single unit. Step 4: Choose the correct combination based on the sentence context. Step 5: Check the correct placement of the object. Example: 'put up with' = tolerate. Sentence: 'She had to put up with the noise.'

sections.title: Double Fillers (Two Phrasal Verbs in One Sentence)
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the overall meaning of the sentence. Step 2: Identify the logical role of both blanks separately. Step 3: Choose the correct phrasal verb for the first blank. Step 4: Select another phrasal verb for the second blank that fits the context. Step 5: Ensure both verbs together create a logical sentence meaning. Example: 'He ran out of money and had to cut down on expenses.'

sections.title: Obscure or Less Common Phrasal Verbs
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the rare phrasal verb. Step 2: Read the sentence context carefully. Step 3: Estimate the logical meaning from the situation. Step 4: Match it with the options given. Step 5: Confirm the final meaning. Examples: pan out = succeed, bear out = confirm, tide over = survive a difficult situation.

sections.title: Error Spotting in Complex Sentences
sections.content: Step 1: Read the sentence structure carefully. Step 2: Identify the particle of the phrasal verb. Step 3: Check whether the particle is placed correctly. Step 4: Verify whether the correct particle has been used. Step 5: Form the corrected structure. Example: 'She is looking forward the trip.' is incorrect. Correct: 'She is looking forward to the trip.'

sections.title: Context and Structural Analysis
sections.content: At Level 3, simply memorizing meanings is not sufficient. In many cases, the correct usage of a phrasal verb depends on both the sentence structure and the context. Therefore, it is important to read the entire sentence carefully.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Forgetting one particle in three-part phrasal verbs. 2. Choosing unrelated verbs for both blanks in double filler questions. 3. Assuming incorrect meanings for rare phrasal verbs. 4. Placing the particle in the wrong position.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 phrasal verbs involve advanced structures such as three-part verbs, double fillers, and rare expressions. Carefully checking context, sentence structure, and particle placement helps in selecting the correct answer.

tricks.title: Three-word Unit Trick
tricks.explanation: Always remember three-part phrasal verbs as a single unit.

tricks.title: Context Pair Trick
tricks.explanation: In double blank questions, both phrasal verbs should logically connect with each other.
tricks.example: Run out of money and cut down on spending.

tricks.title: Rare Verb Memory
tricks.explanation: Memorize uncommon phrasal verbs that often appear in advanced comprehension.

tricks.title: Particle Accuracy Rule
tricks.explanation: Many phrasal verbs require a specific particle for the correct meaning.
tricks.example: Look forward to (not look forward for).

tricks.title: Meaning + Structure Check
tricks.explanation: While choosing the answer, check both the meaning and the grammatical structure.

tricks.title: Error Spotting Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If the particle is missing or incorrect, that is usually the error in the sentence.

tricks.title: Logical Flow Trick
tricks.explanation: Understand the logical flow of the sentence before selecting the phrasal verb.
tricks.example: The plan did not pan out.

tricks.title: Survival Meaning Trick
tricks.explanation: Identify phrasal verbs that indicate surviving or overcoming difficult situations.
